newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Vranitzky urges Albania govt to talk with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky urges Albania govt to talk with rebels.

text.p: The Albanian government and rebel leaders controlling the south should start talks paving the way for new elections, an international mediator said on Wednesday as first emergency aid reached the anarchic Balkan nation.
Franz Vranitzky, envoy for the Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), told leaders of a crisis government formed last month it was time to start talks with the rebel leaders.

"If there are obstacles in a political system, it doesn't help just to ignore them," Vranitzky said. "We think it will be necessary for (the rebels and the government) to have at least a minimum of dialogue between themselves."

Vranitzky, former Austrian chancellor, plans to meet local authorities in the rebel-held south for the first time on Thursday in a move criticised by President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party and conservative Tirana newspapers.

About 300 people have been killed and 700 injured in weeks of chaotic unrest that swept Europe's poorest nation after fraudulent investment schemes collapsed, wiping out the savings of thousands of Albanian families.
Around a million rifles and other weapons were stolen by rebel gangs and ordinary Albanians from armouries left undefended when soldiers and police deserted their posts.
Vranitzky's proposed journey to the southern city of Vlore comes at a delicate time.

A multinational security force that began fanning out through central Albania after arriving on Tuesday to protect movement of humanitarian aid has secured the western port of Durres and Tirana airport.
But the force of more than 1,200 has not yet reached Vlore, the country's second most important harbour and most dangerous city.
There was fresh violence in Vlore on Tuesday night. Police said gunmen fired on a hotel housing foreign journalists and escaped after a 45-minute gunbattle with hotel security.

Police and workers at the Hotel Bologna said two cars filled with gunmen opened fire from the street. No one was injured. Several guests, who took cover in a central hallway, were journalists. Five Italians, one German, and two Lebanese are registered guests at the hotel.
Also in Vlore, police said a man threw a hand grenade at a former army officer after the two had argued. One person was killed and four others seriously injured.
Authorities in the central town of Elbasan said 15 were injured when a grenade exploded in a cemetery during a funeral for a man killed in a gunfight on Sunday.

In the northern town of Skhoder, special police forces confiscated a large number of weapons in a coordinated pre-dawn raid. Dozens of suspects, including police officers and escaped convicts, were arrested, state-run ATA news agency said.

Albanians were pinning their hopes on the 6,000-strong eight-nation force arriving over the next three weeks. The government believes the troops will stabilise the country even though their mission is limited to protecting aid convoys.

Nearly 1,200 troops from Italy, France and Spain landed to start the mission on Tuesday and secured two key bridgeheads at Durres port and Tirana airport. The first 120 of 700 Greek troops reached Albania on Wednesday.
Forces from Turkey, Romania, Austria and Denmark are due to arrive over the next three weeks.
"Everyone seems to be quite happy to see us here," said French army captain Frank Parrera whose unit was inspecting the bridges and roads between Tirana and Durres.
The biggest food shipment to Albania since the launch of the relief mission was unloaded from the Greek-owned ship Stavros Emmanuel in Durres on Wednesday.
About 400 tonnes of wheat flour and beans were lifted off the boat, which had sailed from Italy. The supplies were moved to a port warehouse and could be distributed on Friday.

Relief agencies estimate that one in 10 Albanians needs humanitarian aid. The Geneva-based International Committee of the Red Cross, which does not rely on armed escorts, has been distributing food and medicines since last month.
